picks.title: Can AI make mathematics more human?
picks.excerpt: Mathematician and physicist Yang-Hui He argues that AI is fundamentally reshaping mathematical work — and that the shift pushes mathematicians toward taste, conjecture and meaning rather than away from them. He also says AI creates a new common language that gets estranged subfields talking again, and reports that in FrontierMath's fourth phase the models cracked about 10% of freshly invented problems within a month.
picks.rationale: A working mathematician's account of what AI actually changes in research practice — not a single result headline, but the shift in what the human is for, argued from inside FrontierMath.

picks.title: MIT neuroscientists discover the brain can reason without words
picks.excerpt: MIT researchers found that language and logical reasoning run on separate brain systems: people with severe stroke-induced language impairment still solved hard logic puzzles, while scans showed language regions staying quiet. A pointed empirical challenge to the assumption that language models are reasoning models.
picks.rationale: Direct empirical pressure on the premise underlying LLMs — that fluency and reasoning are the same faculty; the brain says they are not.

picks.title: New AI model detects hidden signs of solar eruptions hours before they emerge
picks.excerpt: NJIT researchers built a Transformer model called EarlyDetect that spots precursor signals of solar active-region emergence in helioseismic acoustic power and magnetic-field data from NASA's SDO, forecasting their appearance an average of 9.24 hours in advance. Removing a noise-filtering step made it better — the filter had averaged away the faint fluctuations that carried the earliest warning.
picks.rationale: Turns helioseismic noise no human forecaster can read into an actionable space-weather warning, and the key finding is a lesson about AI practice: the conventional preprocessing step was destroying the signal.

picks.title: AI-assisted grant proposals may win more often—while narrowing research ideas
picks.excerpt: A Northwestern University study found NIH proposals showing stronger signs of AI-assisted writing were about four percentage points more likely to be funded — but they also resembled previously funded work more closely. The finding suggests LLM drafting quietly steers science toward safer, more conventional questions.
picks.rationale: Quantifies the hidden cost of drafting with an LLM: it raises your hit rate while pulling your ideas toward the mean — an effect anyone writing with AI tomorrow should price in.

picks.title: New AI chip mimics the human brain's capacity for split-second motor control — it solved problems using 10,000 times fewer calculations
picks.excerpt: A brain-inspired device only fires when it detects something unusual, solving control problems with roughly 10,000x fewer calculations than a conventional approach. The neuroscience-to-silicon route is pitched as a way off the power-guzzling data-center dependency.
picks.rationale: A four-order-of-magnitude compute reduction from copying how neurons actually fire — the strongest current argument that the way off the power curve is architectural, not bigger data centers.
